q: A public web server becomes unresponsive after being flooded with simultaneous, overwhelming traffic originating from thousands of geographically dispersed, compromised hosts controlled by a central command server. Which attack is occurring?
exp: A distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack uses multiple compromised endpoints (a botnet) to exhaust a target's system resources or network bandwidth, denying availability to legitimate users.

wrongFeedback.0: A man-in-the-middle (on-path) attack intercepts or alters communications between two legitimate parties rather than overwhelming a host with high-volume traffic.
wrongFeedback.1: Server-side request forgery coerces a server into initiating unauthorized network requests to internal resources, rather than taking a server offline via distributed traffic floods.
wrongFeedback.3: DNS poisoning corrupts name resolution cache entries to redirect client traffic to fraudulent destinations, rather than knocking a server offline through sheer request volume.
